Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 8. октобар ст. ст., „Св. муч. Пелагија“ — Св. is «saint» and not a rank and муч. is the martyr grade this corpus puts in `types`, so both come off and the bare forename is the whole of the form. **The Prologue gives her no epithet either**, so this folder and `pelagia-of-antioch` take the same string from the same page, as they already do for the Russian «Пелагия»; the three-folder fold is read in the `serbian` row’s note and in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`.

death.note: Two calendars give two years and neither is preferred. saint.gr's head line is «Αγια Πελαγια η Παρθενος (; - 284)» with «στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Νουμεριανού 282 - 284 μ.Χ.» in the life; days.pravoslavie.ru's day line prints «Св. Пелагии девы (303)». The interval spans both.

Her line is in the day's second paragraph, which carries no icon; the day's one icon is the plain one and it stands before the first line of the day, which is the other Pelagia's. The line marks her «Св.», holy, rather than «Мц.», martyr, where her index page heads her «Пелагия Антиохийская, дева, мч.» — the day line and the index differ on that word.

Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.10.2026 (8. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Пелагија“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. THE VIRGIN, AND THE PROLOGUE IS THE BOOK THAT SEPARATES HER FROM THE DAY’S FIRST ENTRY BY RANK: муч. here against Преп. there, a martyr against a venerable, two entries on one page. She is of a notable family of Antioch, taken under the emperor Numerian: the folder that exists. `types_add: ["martyr"]`, AND IT IS THE ONLY FIELD THIS DAY ADDED TO ANY FOLDER. **The rank word is in the heading** — Св. муч., martyr by §5 — where the folder held `virgin` alone, taken from saint.gr’s «η Παρθένος». This is not a rank inferred from a verb in a body: it is printed in the heading, which is what §5 counts. The folder’s own life already records that the Russian day line marks her «Св.» while her index entry heads her «мч.», and this book settles which of the two the Serbian prints. `dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE REASON IS A STANDING REFUSAL. The entry dates her only «У време цара Нумеријана», in the time of the emperor Numerian — **an emperor in a life is not a source for a year** — and the folder already carries 284 or 303, the interval that holds saint.gr’s 284 under Numerian and the Russian day line’s 303. The appended paragraph carries no four-digit year at all; this folder has no `birth`, so `date-audit`’s `stated` reads its prose. Measured after the write: `stated` unmoved. WHAT IS NEW, AND ONE PIECE OF IT IS A DIFFERENT DEATH. Three things. She **pretended to be cheerful** and asked the soldiers to wait a moment while she went up to change her clothes. She went up **on the roof of the house**, raised her hands to heaven and prayed a long while that God would take her soul and not let her virgin purity be defiled. And then — «И Бог јој прими душу, а тело паде мртво пред војнике» — **God received her soul, and the body fell dead before the soldiers**. In this account she does not throw herself at all: the Greek page has her open a window and cast herself into the void and be mortally injured, and the Russian article has her go to the place in the house where she used to pray. **The books differ on how she died and the folder is not this reader’s to decide between them**, so the appended paragraph says what this book says and names the difference. THIRD AND LARGEST: **the Prologue quotes the encomium the Greek page only mentions.** saint.gr says no more than that John Chrysostom wrote a celebrated encomium for her; this book prints two sentences of it — that her death was the instrument not of a natural fall but of the commandment of God, and that this virgin body, purer than any gold, lay on the earth with angels about it, archangels honouring it, and Christ himself beside it. `related` UNTOUCHED: `john-chrysostom` is already there and is the only person of the entry with a folder; the governor of Antioch and the soldiers take no rows, and an emperor in a life is not a relation. No `locations`, no `office`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE FOLD THIS DAY MADE, AND IT IS THREE FOLDERS. The Prologue gives **neither** Pelagia an epithet — the two headings are «Преп. Пелагија» and «Св. муч. Пелагија» — so the bare forename is what the source gives and both folders take the same string, the way both already share the Russian «Пелагия». `foldchk.py` measured «Пелагија» **before** this day as `[('pelagia-of-caesarea-in-palestine', 'sr')]` — one folder already held it, off the Prologue’s own heading for the Julian 25 March, so this day widens the fold from one folder to three and not from nothing to two. The READ_FOLDS key `пелагија pelagia-of-antioch pelagia-of-caesarea-in-palestine pelagia-the-virgin-of-antioch` is added to `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` in the same commit, because reading a fold is two acts.
